name: Annular Atrophic Lichen Planus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Annular Atrophic Lichen Planus

criteria.description: Presence of annular, atrophic, violaceous plaques with raised borders
Skin biopsy showing lichenoid interface dermatitis with basal cell degeneration and epidermal atrophy
Exclusion of other annular dermatoses such as tinea corporis or granuloma annulare
Direct immunofluorescence showing fibrinogen deposition along the basement membrane zone

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions plus confirmatory histopathology and exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; immunofluorescence is supportive but not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Annular violaceous plaques with raised borders and central atrophy
searchTerms: ring-shaped purple plaques with raised edges
annular purple skin patches with central thinning
violaceous rings with central skin loss

pathognomonic.symptomName: Lichenoid papules coalescing into annular configurations
searchTerms: lichen planus-like papules merging into circles

common.symptomName: Pruritus localized to affected skin areas

searchTerms: thinning of skin in lesion centers
epidermal thinning in middle of spots

common.symptomName: Hyperpigmentation or post-inflammatory hypopigmentation in lesion sites
searchTerms: dark or light skin changes after lesions
hyperpigmentation or hypopigmentation at lesion sites
Wickham striae at skin lesion margins
fine white streaks around skin spots

occasional.symptomName: Mucosal involvement with white reticular streaks
occasional.notes: Less common than in classic lichen planus
searchTerms: white lacy streaks in mouth lining
mucosal involvement with white net-like patterns

occasional.symptomName: Nail changes including longitudinal ridging or thinning

searchTerms: hair loss with scarring on scalp

rare.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as low-grade fever or malaise

laboratory: Negative fungal cultures to exclude dermatophytosis
other: Skin biopsy showing lichenoid interface dermatitis with basal cell degeneration and epidermal atrophy
Direct immunofluorescence with fibrinogen deposition along basement membrane

distinguishingFeatures: Classic polygonal, flat-topped violaceous papules without annular atrophic configuration
Absence of central atrophy in lesions
Fungal elements on KOH preparation or culture
Scaling and central clearing with active border
Non-itchy, flesh-colored to erythematous annular plaques
Histology showing dermal granulomatous inflammation without lichenoid features

redFlags: Rapid progression of lesions with ulceration
Development of squamous cell carcinoma within chronic lesions
Severe mucosal involvement causing dysphagia or airway compromise
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
